GUIDELINES FOR THE REGISTRATION OF VOTERS,
REVISION AND CONTINUOUS UPDATING OF THE
NATIONAL REGISTER OF VOTERS
PREAMBLE:
WHEREAS the Constitution of the Federal
Republic of Nigeria 1999 empowers the
Independent National Electoral Commission
(herein referred to as the Commission) to
conduct the registrations of persons qualified to
vote and to prepare, maintain and revise the
register of voters;
AND WHEREAS the Electoral act empowers the
Commission to issue regulations, guidelines or
manuals for the purpose of the conduct of the
registration of voters and revision of the register
of voters.
NOW THEREFORE the Commission hereby issues
these guidelines for the registration of voters,
and the updating and revision of the National
Register of Voters.
PART 1: GENERAL REGISTRATION OF
VOTERS

1. The Commission shall, before the date
fixed for general registration of voters,
issue a public notice or announcement
stating:
a) The dates when the general
NOTICE OF
GENERAL

registration of voters shall take place; and
b) The time fixed for the general
registration. 2. (1) The general registration of voters
shall be carried out at such times
and at such centres within the
Federal Republic of Nigeria as may
be designated by the Commission. (2) The list of such centres for each
Local Government Area/ Area
Council shall be displayed at the
Commission's office in that area at
least 7 days before the
commencement of registration. (3) The Commission may use as
registration centres such public
places as schools, halls, parks,
open spaces and booths approved
by the Commission provided that
these registration centres are sited
in the premises of churches,
mosques, palaces of traditional
rulers, political party offices, club
houses, petrol filling stations or
private residential premises. 3.

churches,
mosques, palaces of traditional
rulers, political party offices, club
houses, petrol filling stations or
private residential premises. 3. (1) The registration of voters shall last
for a period as may be determined
by the Commission
(2) During this period, registration
shall begin daily in all registration
centres at 9a.m and end at 3p.m. CENTRES

(3) No person shall be accepted for
registration after 3p.m except
those who are already on the
queue before that time.
4.
(1) A person qualified for registration
shall present himself to the
Registration Officer of the
Commission at the registration
centre.
(2) The Registration Officer:
a) May demand from the applicant
any information as may be required
to enable the officer ascertain
whether the applicant is qualified
to register as a voter, or
b) May require the voter to surrender
any previously issued voters' card
or slip to the registration officer
(3) The voter shall comply with any of
the provisions of paragraph 4 of
these guidelines as may be
required by the Registration
Officer.
5.
(1) Every person who is qualified for
registration and who has presented
himself within the period stipulated
by the Commission for registration
shall be registered in the Preliminary
Register of Voters with the following
PERIOD OF
PRESENTATION

particulars:
a) The registered voter's name;
b) The registered voter's age;
c) The registered voter's sex;
d) The registered voter's occupation;
e) Address within the area;
f) The registered voter's number;
g) The registered voter's photograph;
h) The name of the State where
registration is taking place
i) The name of the Local Government
Area/Area Council of registration
j) Name and code number of the
registration unit
k) The registered voter's thumb
and/or finger print
l) National identity card number
(where available)
(2) The registration officer shall issue the
person whose name and particulars
have been entered on the Preliminary
Register of Voters a voters slip or
card containing the person's name
and particulars

6. No person shall register in more than one
registration centre or register more than
once in the same registration centre
7. (1) The Preliminary Register of Voters
shall be displayed at each registration
centre at such times as the Commission
may direct in form EC1A. The Register
shall be clearly marked Preliminary
Register of Voters.
(2) The display of Preliminary Register of
FOR

Voters shall be carried out in a manner
which affords easy and unimpeded
inspection of the Register by members of
the public.
(3) During the period of display,
members of the public shall be
allowed to inspect the Register free of
charge
(4) Any person caught tampering with
the Preliminary Register of Voters
during the period of display shall be
arrested and prosecuted
(5) At the end of the display period, the
Commission shall effect all necessary
corrections and proceed to produce a
final Register of voters.

8. (1) Within the period allowed by the
Commission for display of the Register,
any person qualified for registration as a
voter, may, if his name is omitted, or is
incorrectly stated in the register, claim in
writing in form EC to have his name
inserted or to have any such entry,
correction or any other omission inserted.
(2) Any person may by notice in writing
in Form EC3, object to the inclusion of
any name appearing in the
Preliminary Register on the ground
that the person:
a) is not a citizen of Nigeria; or
b) has not attained the age of 18
years; or
PARTICULARS OF

c) is not ordinarily resident or work
in, or originate from or an
indigene of that area; or
d) is dead; or
e) is legally incapacitated to vote.

9. (1) A person whose voters' slip or card is
lost, or torn or defaced shall, at least, 7
days to the polls apply to the Commission
for issuance of a duplicate Voters' slip or
Card
(2) An application in sub-paragraph (1) of
this paragraph shall be accompanied by:
a) Proof of identity
b) A processing fee as may be
determined from time to time by the
Commission
(3) An Applicant who satisfies the
provisions of sub-paragraph (2) of
this paragraph and whose name
appears on the register of voters
shall be issued with a duplicate copy
of voters slip or card clearly marked
'Duplicate'.

10.(1) An application for transfer of a
registered voter shall be made to the
Resident Electoral Commissioner in the
State where the voter is currently resident
in form ECTF, 01 not later than 30 days
before the date of the next election.
PROHIBITION OF
MULTIPLE
DISPLAY OF
PRELIMINARY
REGISTER OF
VOTERS

(2) Where a transfer is effected under
sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph, the
voter shall surrender the voter's slip or
card issued to him to the Resident
Electoral Commissioner of the State or the
Electoral Officer of the Local Government
Area/Area Council where he is currently
resident and where the application is
made.
(3) The applicant's name and particulars
shall be entered in the Transferred Voters
Register and he or she shall be issued with
new voter's slip or card indicating the
polling station in a registration area within
the constituency.
(4) The voter's name shall thereafter be
struck off the Register of Voters for
that constituency in which he had
previously registered.

11.(1) Where the registration officer is not
satisfied that a person who presents
himself for registration is qualified, the
Registration Officer shall issue to that
person a notice of rejection in Form ECTF,
02 stating the reason s for rejection
(2) The Registration Officer shall
maintain a record showing the names
and other particulars of every person
whose registration has been rejected
by him pursuant to subparagraph (1)
of this paragraph.
CLAIMS AND
OBJECTIONS

12.(1) Any person who is aggrieved by a
rejection or any decision of the
Registration Officer may appeal to the
Electoral Officer in the Local Government
Area/Area Council of registration at such
time and in such manner as may, by
notice, be prescribed by the Commission.
(2) The Commission shall by notice
inform the public, of the time and
manner in which appeals against
rejections may be made.
(3) The Electoral Officer shall determine
whether or not the Appeal has merit
and if the appeal has merit, a voter's
slip or card shall be issued to the
person who appealed and his name
and shall be entered in the register of
voters.
(4) A record shall be kept of all appeals
that are rejected by the Electoral
Officer and the results of the
determination of all appeals shall be
posted at the Local Government
Area/Area Council of the Commission.

13.(1) Every Political Party, may by notice in
writing signed and addressed to the
Electoral Officer of the Local Government
Area/Area Council, appoint not more than
two agents to attend at each registration
ISSUANCE OF
DUPLICATE
VOTERS,
SLIP/CARD

centre in the Local Government Area/Area
Council. The Notices shall set out the
names and addresses of the agents and be
given to the Electoral Officer before the
date fixed for the registration.
(2) A party agent shall not interfere with
the registration exercise

14.(1) Observers and journalists duly
accredited by the Commission may be
permitted into any registration centre by
the Registration Officer to observe any
registration exercise.
(2) All accredited observers and
journalists shall subscribe to the Code
of Conduct for accredited observers
and journalists and obey all rules and
regulations issued by the
Commission.

15.(1) The Registration Officer or the
Electoral Officer shall be at liberty to order
any Party Agent, Observer, Journalist or
any other person interfering with the
registration process or whose behaviour is
inimical to the smooth conduct of the
exercise to leave the registration centre
and the person so ordered shall comply
forthwith.
(2) A political party or an accredited
observer or media organization may be
allowed to replace its representative so
ordered to leave a registration centre
TRANSFER OF
REGISTERED
VOTER

16. Police officers or other security
officials shall be permitted to enter or
remain in a registration centre by the
Registration Officer and shall be subject to
the direction of the Registration Officer or
Electoral Officer at the registration centre.
PART II- UPDATE OF THE NATIONAL
REGISTER OF VOTERS

17. (1) For the purposes of the
continuous update of the Register of
voters, the Commission shall open a
register at every Local Government
Area/Area Council of the Federation.
(2) Updating of the register shall take
place between the hours of 9a.m and 3p.m
daily on working days.
(3)During this period any Nigerian who
attains the age of 18 years shall present
himself to the Electoral Officer of that
Local Government Area/Area Council and
apply in form EC 1-U for his name to be
included in the Register of voters.
(4) A person seeking to be registered as a
voter during this exercise shall also submit
to the Electoral Officer any of the
following:
a) Proof of age and identity Or
b) National Identity Card where available
REJECTION OF
APPLICATION TO
REGISTER

or any other form of identification
acceptable to the updating officer
(5) Where the updating Officer is satisfied
that the person seeking to have his name
included in the register is qualified, he
shall cause the name and particulars to be
entered in the National Register of Voters.
(6)The updating officer shall thereafter
issue the applicant with a voter's slip or
card.
(7) For the purposes of the updating
exercise, the Electoral Officers shall serve
as updating officers.
PART III: REVISION OF THE NATIONAL
REGISTER OF VOTERS

18. (1) The revision of the national
Register of Voters shall take place on a
date to be fixed by the Commission.
(2)Whenever the Commission decides to
revise the Register, it shall issue a public
notice stating:
a) The date and time when the revision
of the Register shall take place ; and
b) The location or centres at which the
revision shall take place
(3) The revision shall take place between
the hours of 9a.m and 3p.m throughout
the period allowed by the Commission for
APPEAL AGAINST
REJECTION

the revision.
19. An application for inclusion of any
name in the Register during the revision of
the National Register shall be in Form EC 1
and shall be from any person who has:
a) Not been previously registered;
b) Attained eighteen years of age since
the last update of the register of
voters exercise;
c) Changed abode or constituency or
registration since the last update of
the Register of voters.
20. Any person may by notice in
writing to the revision officer in charge of a
revision centre, in Form EC 3A, report that
a person whose name is on the Register is
dead.

21. The Commission shall have
power to remove any name from the
Register if it is satisfied that:
a) The name has been erroneously or
fraudulently entered in the register; or
b) The name belongs to a dead person;
or
c) The name is by law not entitled to be
on the register.
22. (1) The commission may appoint
officers and assign to such officers any
function or duty in relation to the
registration of voters, updating or revision
of the National Register of Voters.
PARTY AGENTS
OBSERVERS/JOUR
NALISTS

(2)All officers appointed by the
Commission for the purposes of
registration, updating or revision of the
register of voters shall not in the
performance of their functions and duties
be subject to the direction or control of any
other person or authority other than the
Commission.
23. Without prejudice to the provision of
these guidelines, the responsibility of
updating or revision of the Register in each
Local Government Area/Area Council shall
be vested in the Electoral Officer of the
Council subject to the direction and
supervision of the Resident Electoral
Commissioner.

24. Notwithstanding the provisions of
these guidelines, the power of control and
supervision of the registration of voters or
updating or revision of the National
register of voters shall be vested in the
Commission and any rules, regulations,
circulars, directives or instructions given
by the Commission regarding any of these
exercises shall be binding on, and be
complied with by all persons involved
therewith.

25. (1) Where a date has been appointed
by the Commission for the registration of
voters or updating or revision of the
Register of voters and there is reason to
believe that a serious breach of the peace
is likely to occur of the registration or
POWER OF
REGISTRATION/EL
ECTORAL OFFICER
SECURITY
OFFICIALS

updating or revision is proceeded with on
the appointed date, the registration or
updating or revision may be postponed by
the Commission until some other
convenient date to be appointed by the
Commission.
(2) where registration or updating or
revision has started on the appointed date
but, is before the conclusion, substantially
disturbed by an intervening cause, the
registration updating or revision may be
suspended by the Commission and the
Commission shall thereafter appoint a new
date for the continuation of the exercise.

26. The Commission may, at its
discretion, change, extend or alter in any
manner the period, dates or times for
doing anything or taking any step under
these guidelines.
27. Non-compliance with the provisions of
these guidelines shall not invalidate
anything done or step taken pursuant to
the guidelines if non-compliance is, in the
opinion of the Commission not substantial.
